name: OCBC Great Eastern Cashflo Credit Card
highlights: Up to 1.2% Cash Rebate if monthly bill is above S$1,000
Up to 0.3% Cash Rebate if your monthly bill is less than S$1,000
0% Interest when you split your bills into 3, 6 or 12-month instalments
Earn up to 1.2% cash rebate every month
Stretch payments across 3, 6, or 12* months with 0% interest
2 years fee waiver, subsequent years waived with min. spend S$10,000 p.a.

citation.title: OCBC Great Eastern Cashflo Credit Card

minimum-income-requirements.Singaporean/PR Minimum Annual Income:
•At least S$30,000 for Singaporeans and Singapore PRs aged between 21 and 54
•At least S$15,000 for Singaporeans and Singapore PRs aged 55 and above

our_takes.our-take: The OCBC Great Eastern Cashflo card suits Great Eastern policyholders seeking payment flexibility. Its headline 1.2% cashback on spends above S$1,000 is decent, but the sub-1% rate below that threshold is less compelling. The key draw is the 0% interest instalment plan for Great Eastern premiums, easing large payments; however, note the 1% processing fee for 12-month plans. Factor in the S$10,000 annual spend for fee waiver, otherwise, a S$163.50 fee applies. If you're not an existing Great Eastern customer, other general cashback cards likely offer more value.
our_takes.good-for:
Cardholders who want to stretch payments on larger purchases with interest-free installments at select merchants.
Great Eastern policyholders seeking a convenient way to manage and pay their insurance premiums efficiently.
Consumers who spend over S$1,000 monthly, aiming to maximize cashback earnings on their retail expenses.
our_takes.things-to-note:
Cashback is tiered; spending below S$1,000 monthly earns only 0.3%, limiting your rewards significantly for lower spend.
27.78% annual interest rate applies if you don't pay your balance in full; debt can increase rapidly.
S$150 fee applies if you terminate your card or accelerate payments, so consider this before closing the account.
